notes: Weekdays use JavaScript numbering (0 = Sunday). Hours are local clock time, [start, end).
Holidays are not removed from peak windows (a small conservative simplification: it can only overstate billing demand slightly).
kVA / power-factor provisions are not modeled; billing demand is in kW.

Supply (Basic Service) is a flat 14.3 cents/kWh: the 12-month average of National Grid's NEMA fixed industrial Basic Service rate, Nov 2025 - Oct 2026 (M.D.P.U. 1-26-A, -E, -G, -I sheet 5). It only affects the value of energy lost in the battery.

tariffs.label: National Grid G-3
tariffs.description: Massachusetts Electric time-of-use rate for customers averaging over 200 kW.
tariffs.source: M.D.P.U. No. 1-26-I, Summary of Electric Delivery Service Rates, sheet 3 (effective Oct 1, 2026); billing demand per tariff M.D.P.U. No. 1591

demand.name: Distribution demand
demand.rule: Greatest 15-minute kW during peak hours (8 am to 9 pm, Monday to Friday).

tariffs.not_modeled: Transmission is billed per kWh (3.455 cents) on the default option, so it does not respond to shaving. The optional Transmission Coincident Peak charge ($21.91/kW at ISO-NE's monthly peak hour) is discussed separately.

tariffs.label: Eversource G-2, Greater Boston
tariffs.description: NSTAR Electric medium general service, Greater Boston service area, below 14 kV.
tariffs.source: M.D.P.U. No. 1-26-F, Summary of Electric Service Delivery Rates, p. 2 (effective Sept 1, 2026); billing demand per tariff M.D.P.U. No. 15I

demand.name: Distribution + transmission demand
demand.rule: Greatest 15-minute kW in the month, except demand in off-peak hours is reduced by 55%: billed kW = max(peak-period kW, 0.45 x off-peak kW).

tariffs.not_modeled: Customer charge tier uses the highest billing demand of the evaluation year as a stand-in for the trailing 12 months.
